diagnostics.message: :resource.null_resource.wait_for_cluster: explicit depends_on of :resource.aws_eks_cluster.this is redundant — already implied by attribute references

`:resource.null_resource.wait_for_cluster` declares `depends_on = [aws_eks_cluster.this[0]]`, but the provisioner already sets `environment = { ENDPOINT = aws_eks_cluster.this[0].endpoint }`, which creates the very same implicit dependency on `:resource.aws_eks_cluster.this`. The explicit `depends_on` duplicates it and can be dropped.

`:resource.aws_eks_node_group.workers` (module.node_groups) is created with `node_role_arn` pointing at the worker role, but nothing orders it after `:resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.workers_AmazonEKSWorkerNodePolicy`. Per the aws_eks_node_group docs, IAM role permissions must exist before the node group is handled, and before/after deletion, otherwise EKS cannot properly create or delete the underlying EC2 instances and ENIs.

`:resource.aws_eks_node_group.workers` (module.node_groups) has no dependency on `:resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.workers_AmazonEKS_CNI_Policy`. Nodes created by the node group need the CNI policy attached to their role in order to bring up pod networking; without the ordering the group can be provisioned against a role lacking the policy (and deletion can fail for the same reason).

`:resource.aws_eks_node_group.workers` (module.node_groups) has no dependency on `:resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.workers_AmazonEC2ContainerRegistryReadOnly`. The node group's role must already carry the ECR read-only policy when the group is created (and must keep it until the group is deleted), otherwise nodes cannot pull images and EKS teardown can fail.
